topic: How the shipping container changed the world
hook: A plain steel box quietly made almost everything you own cheaper.
on_screen_hook: The steel box that made *everything* cheaper

blocks.narration: A plain steel box quietly made almost everything you own cheaper. It is the shipping container, and it is younger than you think.
blocks.visual: Photoreal aerial shot of a colorful container port at sunrise, cranes moving in unison

blocks.narration: Before the nineteen fifties, ships were loaded by hand. Workers carried sacks, barrels, and crates one at a time, for days.
blocks.visual: Cinematic black and white style shot of dock workers hauling crates up a gangway

blocks.narration: A trucking businessman named Malcom McLean had an idea. Why not lift the entire truck trailer onto the ship?
blocks.visual: A vintage truck trailer is lifted by a crane above a ship's deck, dramatic low angle

blocks.narration: In nineteen fifty-six, his ship, the Ideal X, sailed from Newark to Houston carrying fifty-eight metal containers on its deck, and history quietly changed.
blocks.visual: An old tanker ship with neat rows of boxes on deck sails out of a misty harbor

blocks.narration: Loading cargo by hand had cost about five dollars eighty-three a ton. With containers, it fell to around sixteen cents.
blocks.visual: Two coin piles side by side, one tall, one tiny, under clean studio light

blocks.narration: Standard sizes followed, so the same box could move from ship to train to truck without ever being unpacked.
blocks.visual: A single container glides seamlessly from a ship crane onto a train car, then onto a truck

blocks.narration: Shipping costs collapsed, ports were rebuilt, and global trade exploded. Today, giant ships carry thousands of containers at once.
blocks.visual: A massive modern container ship stacked high with boxes slides past the camera

blocks.narration: One simple steel box rewired the entire world economy. Share this with someone who loves how the world really works.
blocks.visual: Wide drone shot pulls back from the port as lights come on at dusk

cta: Share this with someone who loves how the world really works.

captions.hook_line: A plain steel box quietly made almost everything you own cheaper 📦
captions.body: In 1956, Malcom McLean's Ideal X carried 58 containers from Newark to Houston. Hand-loading cargo cost about $5.83 a ton; loading containers cost around 16 cents a ton, and global trade was never the same.
